fields.value: An amiable, elegant woman; the novel emphasizes manners and intelligence over detailed features.
Warm, perceptive, tactful, sensible, and capable of giving advice without claiming authority.
To care for her nieces, encourage prudent judgment, and preserve trust through honest counsel.
Connected to Derbyshire before marriage and familiar with Lambton and the Pemberley area.
Not stated; an established married adult.
Manages the Gardiner household; no paid occupation stated.
Elizabeth’s trusted adult confidante and the mediator who later explains Darcy’s hidden intervention.
Wife of Mr Gardiner; aunt of the Bennet sisters; mother of several children.
Guides Elizabeth away from imprudent attachment, accompanies her to Pemberley, and delivers the evidence that completes Darcy’s moral revelation.
Elizabeth: affectionate niece and confidante. Darcy: impressed observer. Mr Gardiner: companion in travel and family responsibility.
Chapter 25 during the Christmas visit to Longbourn.
